units.title: Calcium Homeostasis: RANK-RANKL Physiology and Steps of Bone Remodeling
units.sec: Calcium Homeostasis: RANK-RANKL Physiology and Steps of Bone Remodeling · p224
units.guide: PTH and vitamin D3 stimulate osteoblasts to synthesize RANK ligand (Step-I). RANK ligand activates RANK receptor on osteoclast precursors (Step-II), causing structural change with ruffled borders (Step-III) and bone resorption (Step-IV). The resorption triggers osteoblast activation (Step-V) and new bone formation at the injury site (Step-VI). Strontium ranelate is unique with dual action — it increases bone formation and decreases bone resorption.

units.title: Bisphosphonates: MOA and Pharmacology
units.guide: Bisphosphonates inhibit farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase in osteoclasts, leading to apoptosis of osteoclasts. They are the DOC when maximum hypocalcemia is needed. Their oral absorption is poor, so they must be taken on an empty stomach for adequate bioavailability.

units.title: Bisphosphonates: Route, Dosing and Clinical Uses
units.sec: Bisphosphonates: Route, Dosing and Clinical Uses · p225
units.guide: Intravenous bisphosphonates — pamidronate every 3 months and zoledronate preferred, once yearly, longest acting and more potent — are used for 3 years. Oral bisphosphonates — risedronate once daily and alendronate preferred once daily — are used for 5 years. For osteoporosis the DOC is alendronate, and if intolerant switch to zoledronate; for hypercalcemia of malignancy and Paget disease start with zoledronate directly.

units.title: Bisphosphonates: Side Effects and Prevention
units.sec: Bisphosphonates: Side Effects and Prevention · p225
units.guide: Oral bisphosphonates cause esophagitis, prevented by taking the drug with a full glass of water and not lying down for 30 minutes. IV bisphosphonates more commonly cause bone fractures including the characteristic femoral chalk-stick fracture whose DOC is teriparatide, maximum hypercalcemia as a paradox, and osteonecrosis of the jaw shown in the clinical photograph.

units.title: Denosumab, Raloxifene and Calcitonin Analog
units.sec: Denosumab, Raloxifene and Calcitonin Analog · p225
units.guide: Denosumab is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits RANK ligand and is used in postmenopausal osteoporosis. Calcitonin analog is used intranasally for osteoporosis and subcutaneously for Paget disease, but increases the risk of cancer. Raloxifene is a SERM that mimics estrogen action on bone to inhibit resorption.

units.title: Anabolic Drugs and Postmenopausal Osteoporosis Algorithm
units.sec: Anabolic Drugs and Postmenopausal Osteoporosis Algorithm · p226
units.guide: Anabolic drugs build bone: teriparatide is a PTH analog with side effect osteosarcoma, contraindicated in Paget disease and limited to maximum 2 years; abaloparatide is a PTH-related peptide analog; romosozumab inhibits sclerostin. The treatment algorithm for postmenopausal osteoporosis starts with alendronate DOC, if intolerant switch to zoledronate, if still intolerant check fracture risk — high risk gets denosumab and very high risk gets anabolic drugs teriparatide or romosozumab.
